messages:
kevin: Noticing a cluster-level blip in ap-southeast1 around 07:12 UTC. Small GPU pods (<=1 GPU) failing with `AttachNetworkInterfaceError` and then getting preempted. Pattern looks like an intermittent conntrack exhaustion on nodes in rack-r2. Anyone digging in?

tara: I saw that too. Node metrics show conntrack table high ~98% on those nodes and `kubelet` reporting device attach retries. Dashboard: https://grafana/redwood/d/network/conntrack?from=now-1h&var-region=ap-southeast1 :mag:

infra-bot: alert: conntrack-high (ap-southeast1-rack-r2) triggered at 07:13 UTC. affected_nodes: 3. recent pod evictions: 22 in 20m. Suggested remediation: increase nf_conntrack_max, apply conntrack GC tunables.

priya: quick triage: CNI plugin (calico) shows many short-lived connections from init containers hitting conntrack churn. Warmpool handoff amplifies, because attach/detach causes controlplane chatter.

sam: short-term mitigation: cordon the three bad nodes and drain tiny non-critical pods to adjacent racks. That will reduce conntrack pressure. I can run a scoped drain now if we agree.

kevin: agree to targeted drain; do NOT drain the whole node (we want to preserve GPU capacity). Only evict pods labeled `role!=critical && gpu<=1`.

tara: command ready: `kubectl drain node/r2-node-07 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --pod-selector='gpu<=1,role!=critical'` — will run in 2m.

ops-bot: ticket INF-1310 created tracking conntrack spikes, node drains, kernel tunables. assigned: @priya, @sam.

priya: medium-term fix proposals (ranked):
1) bump `net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max` from 262144 -> 524288 on rack-r2 nodes via nodepool image patch.
2) enable aggressive conntrack GC: `net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_tcp_timeout_established=120` and `nf_conntrack_buckets` tuning.
3) add a nightly crm to purge stale conntrack entries for known short-lived ports (temporary safeguard).
4) review CNI and init container networking patterns to reduce ephemeral ports during startup.

kevin: +1 on 1 and 2. Concern: doubling conntrack table increases memory. Need an estimate of memory delta per node.

priya: estimate: approx +50-80MB per node at peak for our workloads if we double nf_conntrack_max. We have headroom on r2 hosts. I'll attach numbers in the ticket.

sam: operational plan: (A) scoped drains immediately (5-10m), (B) patch nodepool image with conntrack sysctl and rollout to r2 only as a canary (30m rollout, monitor), (C) keep a 2-node warmpool buffer for 1h to avoid attach storms during rollout.

infra-bot: telemetry: p95 scheduling latency for 1GPU pods on r2 nodes spiked from 35s -> 120s during peak, eviction rate 0.6% -> 3.4% over 15m.

kevin: let's do it. Sam, start the drains now. Priya, prepare image patch and kubelet/sysctl manifest. Tara, monitor Grafana and drop updates here. I'll be on call for the next 60m.

sam: draining nodes now. Will move only non-critical tiny pods.

tara: watching dashboards. conntrack metrics already dipping on node-07 after eviction wave.

priya: preparing a DaemonSet patch to apply sysctls via `sysctl.d/99-conntrack.conf` and a rollout plan. Example snippet: 

```
# /etc/sysctl.d/99-conntrack.conf
net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=524288
net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_tcp_timeout_established=120
```

kevin: ensure the patch has an automated rollback if memory pressure exceeds threshold. Add a probe that checks `free -m` and `conntrack -S`.

ops-bot: canary job INF-1310-1 scheduled: nodepool patch -> r2 nodes (3 hosts), rollback trigger: mem_avail_percent < 18% or evictions > 1% over 10m.

sam: drains finished. nodes uncordoned after tiny pod placement; GPUs remain available. Immediate improvements visible on node-07.

tara: tracking: p95 scheduling down to 48s now, conntrack table usage 76% -> 64% on patched nodes (after drain).

priya: will post patch PR with baked-in rollback and memory checks in INF-1310. Follow-up: let's audit init containers that open many simultaneous connections on startup for model loaders (cc @mlinfra).

kevin: thanks team. We'll keep this thread as the incident record and close INF-1310 once the canary is safe and we roll the patch to the region.
